edits.role: Initial reduction; still too cupped, not selected
edits.prompt:
Edit the supplied detached alien stone-egg hatch reference. Change ONLY its curvature: make it ALMOST FLAT, an extremely shallow curved shell panel rather than a cupped bowl.

Keep its elongated teardrop-oval outline (narrow tip at left, broad round end at right), pale granite outer edge with a little scorching at the left, warm grey mineral inner face, subtle flush branching alien inlays, narrow dark sealing strip, plain white studio background and single-object photorealistic image-to-3D presentation.

CRITICAL GEOMETRY: reduce the existing concavity by about 90 percent. The hatch is roughly 140 cm long and 75 cm wide but only about 3 cm of total gentle bow across its width. Material thickness is a uniform 1.5 to 2 cm. Almost the entire inner face is a broad, nearly planar surface with a subtle continuous shallow curve. The perimeter is simply the thin edge of this bent sheet of rock; NO raised side walls, no upturned perimeter, no basin, no deep central depression, no thick rim. All points of the perimeter sit close to one plane. It should read as a thin curved flake taken from the side of a much larger egg, or a very slightly dished panel. It is a shell segment, not a container.

Show the slightly concave INNER face toward the viewer, tilted gently for a three-quarter perspective with enough edge visibility to show the thin material and tiny curvature. Camera about 25-30 degrees above the panel surface. The far edge is not a tall wall. The near edge visibly exposes a thin granite cross-section; the underside and a delicate grounding shadow establish that this is a separate shell panel, not a painted solid rock. Use gentle lighting to reveal the shallow curvature without exaggerating depth. Only minute dry/wet clear jelly traces, no pool.

One whole hatch only, centered with generous margins, long axis left to right, no body, no stand, no extra views or objects, no text or labels. Preserve the reference's material identity but strongly prioritize the user's requested ALMOST FLAT shape.

edits.role: Final selected edit of the initial reduction; nearly planar panel
edits.prompt:
Make a major geometry correction to this hatch: FLATTEN IT INTO AN ALMOST PLANAR, THIN STONE SHELL PANEL. The current reference is still far too cupped. Preserve only its surface materials, teardrop-oval outline and embedded alien linework. Do not preserve its bowl shape or camera angle.

The entire object is a thin sheet of mineral shell, 140 cm long by 75 cm wide, with uniform 1 cm thickness and ONLY 1.5 cm of gentle curvature across the full width. Almost perfectly flat. A broad flat inner face extending right up to the thin perimeter, with no sides rising around it. There are ZERO raised sidewalls, ZERO deep cavity, ZERO raised lip or high back edge, and no central depression suggesting a basin. Its silhouette in profile is a very gently bowed line of nearly constant thickness, like a slightly curved flat oval roofing tile. It is an almost flat piece of the shell, not a dish, bowl, boat, tray or vessel.

Show the warm-grey inner face toward the camera. Use a MUCH LOWER, more edge-on three-quarter camera angle, about 18 degrees above the plane of the panel, so the thin side profile is unmistakable while a substantial area of the flat decorated inner surface is visible. The near and far edges must almost line up vertically because the panel is so flat. Long axis left-to-right, narrow end LEFT and broad round end RIGHT. Rest it on the white surface; soft delicate contact shadow only. Rotate its footprint so the long side is nearly broadside to the viewer; strong foreshortening across its width. The whole object should appear low and flattened in the frame, no tall far end.

Keep pale speckled granite on the extremely thin exposed edge and small scorched patch at the left tip; the inner face is warm-grey mineral with restrained flush bronze/ceramic alien branching inlays from the reference. A hairline dark seal follows the edge without sticking up. No liquid pool; at most a tiny faint clear film. One object only on white studio background, photoreal game-prop image-to-3D reference, no text, no second view, no pod body. The most important requirement is ALMOST FLAT, just a very slight shell curvature.
